blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs), including heart disease, diabetes and cancer, accounted for more than half of the Philippines’ health expenditures in 2025, while spending on medicines and medical supplies also increased, highlighting the growing financial demands of managing chronic illnesses. Data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), analyzed by University of the Philippines Diliman associate professor and Inquirer data scientist Dr. Rogelio Alicor Panao, showed that NCDs accounted for 50.5% of health expenditures in 2025, up from 33.9% in 2014.
